text: The giant came out every day and shouted.
His name was Goliath.
Israel heard him, and Israel was afraid.
The armies stood on opposite hills with the valley between them.
The Philistines had their champion.
Israel had soldiers, weapons, and a king, but no man wanted to face Goliath.
The giant knew it.
Goliath kept talking, and no one answered.
The fear spread through the camp.
Saul was king, but he did not go.
Not yet.
David came carrying food for his brothers.
He was young, and he looked like a shepherd because he was one.
He heard defiance against God.
The soldiers heard a giant.
David heard an insult against the living God, and that changed everything.
The men around him talked about Goliath's size, his armor, and his spear.
David talked about God.
David spoke like a man who knew God.
Saul offered David armor, but it did not fit him.
It belonged to another man's way of fighting, so David took it off.
Just trust, courage, and a clean shot.
David walked into the valley.
Goliath saw him coming and mocked him.
He knew what Goliath could see, and he knew what Goliath could not see.
Goliath came forward with his spear and shield.
His armor made him look almost impossible to beat.
His voice was full of contempt.
David answered with faith.
The whole valley seemed to hold its breath.
The stone struck Goliath, and the giant stopped.
Then he fell forward to the ground.
David ran to him, and the battle turned in a moment.
When Goliath fell, the valley changed.
Israel saw it.
God had answered, and courage began to move.
David stood where no one else had wanted to stand.
He had not trusted size, armor, or pride.
He had trusted God.
That was the real victory.
He won because God was with him.
The story was remembered because the giant fell.
But the deeper thing was this: David saw the battle rightly.
And God's people knew the victory belonged to God.
